brief.headline: SK Hynix $1T / KOSPI 50% concentration / HBM sold out through 2027
brief.summary: <cite index="2-19,39-1">SK Hynix crossed $1 trillion market cap on May 27 after surging 14.9%, joining Samsung and Micron in the trillion-dollar club.</cite> <cite index="2-6,2-22">SK Hynix's 2026 HBM capacity is fully sold out, with supply shortages projected into 2027.</cite> <cite index="39-13,39-16">The combined market capitalization of Samsung and SK Hynix surpassed 50.44% of the entire KOSPI for the first time, with 826 decliners versus 77 advancers.</cite> <cite index="11-2,11-7">Conventional DRAM contract prices rose 58-63% QoQ in Q2 2026, while NAND Flash jumped 70-75% QoQ, following Q1's 90-95% DRAM surge.</cite> <cite index="21-5,21-7">Top-5 hyperscalers will spend ~$602B in 2026 capex (+36% YoY), with ~75% ($450B) tied to AI infrastructure.</cite>
brief.pair_trade_view: <cite index="2-7,6-5">SK Hynix has secured 70% market share in HBM4 for Nvidia's Rubin platform in 2026 and dominates HBM3E leadership.</cite> <cite index="41-8">Samsung's HBM4 strategy is showing progress—customers stating 'Samsung is back'—but SK Hynix held 53% of the HBM market in Q3 2025 versus Samsung's 35%.</cite> Samsung is playing catch-up on yield and qualification, creating a structural long-bias toward SK Hynix in near-term relative value. <cite index="39-13,39-20">Sixteen leveraged ETFs tracking both names posted 10.4 trillion won first-day volume and 2.053 trillion won net purchases, amplifying concentration risk.</cite> SK Hynix offers cleaner HBM exposure; Samsung carries foundry/logic diversification but dilutes memory cycle purity. Pair: long SK Hynix, neutral-to-underweight Samsung on a memory-purity basis.

memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="4-1">Goldman Sachs forecasts a 4.9% DRAM supply deficit in 2026.</cite> <cite index="15-22,15-24,15-25">Hyperscaler capex among top 8 CSPs projected to exceed $600B in 2026 (+40% YoY), while HBM is crowding out commodity DRAM capacity with a 3-to-1 conversion ratio between HBM and DDR5 wafer capacity.</cite> <cite index="6-14">BofA forecasts global DRAM revenue to surge 51% and NAND 45% YoY in 2026, with ASPs rising 33% and 26%, respectively.</cite> Pricing momentum moderating from Q1's extreme 90-95% QoQ spike to Q2's 58-63%, but <cite index="15-7">analysts project the memory price rally will extend past 2028.</cite> Cycle differs from historical boom-bust: disciplined capacity adds, structural AI demand floor, and memory as compute bottleneck shift dynamics.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="2-6,2-22">SK Hynix's 2026 HBM capacity is fully sold out, with supply shortages projected into 2027.</cite> <cite index="2-1,2-25">Customers signing HBM contracts now are targeting 2027 delivery windows.</cite> <cite index="6-18,6-19">BofA estimates the 2026 HBM market at $54.6B (+58% YoY), with Goldman forecasting HBM demand for ASIC-based AI chips to skyrocket 82%, accounting for one-third of the market.</cite> <cite index="1-11,1-13">SK Hynix announced iHBM thermal architecture integrating cooling elements inside HBM packages, reducing thermal resistance by over 30%.</cite> <cite index="9-14">HBM rose from 52% to 63% of all AI chip component spending between Q1 2024 and Q4 2025.</cite> <cite index="5-4,5-5">Industry exploring architectural changes to separate GPUs and HBM into different packages connected via optical links to expand memory capacity.</cite> Intel/SoftBank ZAM memory alternative gaining traction but remains years from production.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix crosses $1 trillion market cap, KOSPI hits all-time high
news_pulse.implication: Third memory maker to join trillion-dollar club after Samsung (May 6) and Micron (May 5). Samsung/SK Hynix now 50.44% of KOSPI; extreme index concentration creates systemic risk if HBM demand corrects. VKOSPI fear index hit 70.78—high volatility despite rally.

news_pulse.headline: DRAM prices +58-63% QoQ in Q2 2026, NAND +70-75% QoQ
news_pulse.implication: Follows Q1's record 90-95% DRAM surge. NAND outpacing DRAM for first time this cycle due to enterprise SSD demand. Suppliers reallocating to AI/server, starving PC/mobile. Pricing pressure extends through 2027-2028 per consensus.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler 2026 capex reaches $602-725B, 75% AI-focused
news_pulse.implication: Big Four (AMZN, MSFT, GOOGL, META) each exceeding $100B annually. Microsoft cited $25B memory inflation impact. Structural demand floor for HBM/DRAM but investor ROI skepticism rising—hyperscaler shares sold off post-earnings despite record capex guidance.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS capacity ramping to 120-130K wafers/month by end-2026
news_pulse.implication: Nearly quadrupling from 35K in late 2024. Nvidia secured ~60% of 2026 allocation; Broadcom 15%, AMD 11%. CoWoS bottleneck easing but remains gating factor for HBM-GPU integration. TSMC outsourcing 240-270K wafers/year to Amkor/SPIL.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix unveils iHBM thermal tech, 30% thermal resistance reduction
news_pulse.implication: Integrated cooling elements in D2D PHY layer target HBM5 (2029+). Addresses thermal constraints as memory becomes the compute bottleneck. Reinforces SK Hynix's technology leadership runway beyond HBM3E/HBM4.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung/SK Hynix leveraged ETFs debut; 16 products see 10.4T won volume
news_pulse.implication: 2x leveraged single-stock ETFs launched May 27. Net purchases of 2.053T won first day. Margin balances: Samsung 4.2T won, SK Hynix 3.3T won (up 2.4x and 3.4x YTD). Amplifies retail speculation and volatility risk into already concentrated index.

news_pulse.headline: Memory cyclicality debate: investors warn of boom-bust risk
news_pulse.implication: Samsung +114% YTD, SK Hynix +186%, Micron +141%, SanDisk +156%. Deutsche Bank flags TurboQuant AI inference technique as potential structural demand disruptor. JM Finn notes production can increase meaningfully over 3 years if AI demand normalizes—current prices assume extended high-price regime and capital discipline.

news_pulse.headline: Industry exploring GPU-HBM separation via optical links
news_pulse.implication: Korean memory makers discussing placing GPUs and HBM in separate packages connected via optical interconnects to expand capacity beyond current stacking limits. Architectural shift could enable several times more HBM per GPU but requires photonic miniaturization. OSAT players monitoring closely.

brief.derivatives_signal: <cite index="39-17,43-5">VKOSPI (KOSPI 200 Volatility Index) closed at 70.78 (+3.95% from prior day), spiking intraday to 82.23.</cite> Levels above 40 indicate fear zone; current reading comparable to Iran war outbreak. Extreme divergence: KOSPI at all-time high but index moving inversely with volatility—typically they move opposite. <cite index="43-8,43-9">Korea Investment & Securities notes unusual simultaneous surge in stock index and volatility index.</cite> Implies hedging demand amid concentrated long exposure. <cite index="43-10,43-11,43-12,43-13">Margin balances: Samsung 4.2T won, SK Hynix 3.3T won—up 2.4x and 3.4x respectively YTD.</cite> Elevated put skew likely; consider selling OTM puts on dips or calendar spreads to harvest elevated IV. Risk: leveraged ETF cascade if either name corrects sharply.
